SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-14 first issue, which defined option A as a 'non-scratch root' without saying what makes a root non-scratch. The census emits only the path string, so two readers could produce different denominators from identical output -- the predicate was not in fact census-computable, which is the constraint it was selected for. Fixed by requiring an explicit admitted-root set fixed before observation.

SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-14 second issue, which carried 'estate-armed-count-remains-zero' as a validity condition. Option A references receipts and admitted-root membership only; the zero-armed count is DATED EVIDENCE (census run 2026-08-13) bearing on option D via d3, not a standing condition on the selected option. As a validity condition it would void the governing record the moment a mission armed -- and arming is a positive envelope-adoption event this window exists to measure, so the first interesting datapoint would have destroyed the rule it arrived under.

A nonzero armed count during the window retires d3's SECOND line of evidence against option D ('guard-referencing predicates are already empty'), but not d1's refutation of D, which is structural (selection on the dependent variable) and does not depend on any estate observation. The selection of A therefore stands under a nonzero armed count.

SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-14 third issue on two counts. (a) valid_while carried 'census-computable-field-set-unchanged', which the very commit publishing this record falsified: it adds epoch_skew to every census report relative to the pinned revision, so the record voided the moment it landed and before its window could open. Narrowed to the fields option A and the numerator actually read. (b) The numerator was left as the unglossed phrase 'a populated envelope' while the denominator was specified to the field -- the same defect as the original 'non-scratch root', on the other half of the ratio.

SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-14 fourth issue on two counts. (a) The denominator was restricted to ACTIVE missions, so ordinary completion during the 60-day interval removed missions from both numerator and denominator -- the closing ratio would have been computed over long-lived survivors, and could have been empty while many qualifying missions adopted the envelope and finished. Survivorship selection, in a record whose P8 coverage exists to catch exactly that. (b) The prerequisite test passed on a census reporting answers_are_partial == true, so the window could open on a selectively incomplete estate whose skipped stores are precisely the ones whose contribution is unknown.

SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-14 fifth issue on three counts. (a) empirical_premises asserted the non-emptiness result flatly while coverage_limits said the estate was unreachable and empirical_closure said pending -- a consumer reading premises as established would treat the prerequisite as already satisfied. (b) The close was fixed at 2026-10-13 while the opening became 'planned', so a late open silently shortened the observation with no rule governing it. (c) The round-4 cohort fix handled TOTAL attrition (empty closing denominator) and not PARTIAL: with two members and one disappearance the recovery never fires, and because the opening record kept only identity, an adopted mission could vanish and move the reported ratio from 1/2 to 0/1. The opening record now captures adoption state, and partial attrition has its own rule.

SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-14 sixth issue. The round-5 partial-attrition rule said a disappeared member's adoption counts 'on the strength of the opening-cohort record' -- but a member that adopts AFTER opening and then disappears is recorded pre-adoption in that snapshot and is gone from the closing census, and no observation cadence was required anywhere. The rule therefore asserted an observation capability that did not exist. Interval re-observation is now required and must be persisted, and the cadence's resolution limit is recorded as a concession rather than glossed.

SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-14 seventh issue on two counts. (a) The cadence re-observed only the OPENING cohort, so a mission created during the interval -- or one gaining its first chain-bound receipt -- had no admission rule and could be omitted entirely, biasing the ratio toward the opening population while the model said the cohort is every qualifying mission observed at any point. (b) The partial-attrition rule counted a vanished member's later-observed adoption while the reporting rule computed the full-cohort ratio from opening state, so one observation history yielded two different numerators depending on which rule the reader followed.

>=1 chain-bound receipt AND a root drawn from the ADMITTED-ROOT SET recorded at window open (an explicit list of repository checkouts, fixed before observation begins).
Envelope-referencing predicate (e.g. armed missions, or missions with non-empty scope).

assumptions: The gate owner judges adoption from census output rather than by inspection of each mission.
authorized_objectives: Make the es#166 adoption question measurable rather than unmeasurable (es#150 ruling).
Prevent the freeze becoming null-by-drift at window close (es#150 ruling time-box).
empirical_premises: PENDING OBSERVATION, not established: candidate A selects a non-empty set of missions on the live estate. The live estate is unreachable from the session that produced this record; this is the hypothesis the preregistered test in empirical_closure exists to check, and the window does not open until that test passes on a complete census run. A consumer must NOT read this list as a set of verified facts.
hard_constraints: Computable by the census from fields it already reports.
The predicate must not be defined in terms of the variable whose adoption it measures.
The predicate must select a non-empty set on the live estate, or the window is vacuous by construction.
Membership must be reproducible from census output plus the recorded admitted-root set, with no per-reader judgement about what a root 'is'.

The NUMERATOR predicate ('populated envelope') is fixed and recorded before observation begins, exactly as the denominator is; a ratio with a reproducible denominator and a reader-chosen numerator is not reproducible.
The cohort is fixed by OBSERVATION over the interval, not by lifecycle state at the closing read: a mission satisfying the predicate counts whether it is active or terminal when observed.

Every census run bearing on this measurement -- the prerequisite and the close -- must report answers_are_partial == false. A partial run has silently omitted stores from both numerator and denominator.
decision_frame.question: Which census-computable predicate defines a 'substantive mission' for the es#166 adoption window such that envelope adoption is actually measurable and the measurement is not controlled by the party being measured?
decision_frame.system_boundary: mission-custody@1 stores discoverable by census_missions.py under operator-named roots. The es#166 adoption window is PLANNED, opening only when the non-emptiness precondition passes, and closing 2026-10-13. THE CLOSE DOES NOT MOVE: it is the calendar deadline the es#150 ruling requires, and sliding it to preserve a 60-day interval is the null-by-drift that ruling forbids. A late open therefore SHORTENS the observation rather than delaying the judgement, and the interval is governed explicitly in synthesis.conditions.

derivations.construct: selection on the dependent variable invalidates the estimate
derivations.counterexample: Under D with predicate 'guard_mode is not null', an estate that goes from 1 armed mission to 1 armed mission and 40 unarmed empty-envelope missions reports p = 1 both before and after, while adoption has measurably worsened.

derivations.model: The window estimates p = NUMERATOR / DENOMINATOR over the WINDOW COHORT: every mission satisfying the selected predicate that is OBSERVED at any point in the interval, whether active or terminal when observed. The cohort is deliberately NOT 'missions active at the closing read': a mission that adopted the envelope and then completed would leave both numerator and denominator, so ordinary completion could empty the denominator or bias it toward long-lived survivors -- survivorship selection, on the same P8 family this record fired on. DENOMINATOR = missions satisfying the selected predicate (option A). NUMERATOR = those denominator missions with a POPULATED ENVELOPE, defined exactly as: scope_in non-empty OR scope_out non-empty OR guard_count > 0 -- the three envelope fields the census actually reports. 'Populated envelope' was previously left to the reader, which let identical census output yield different values of p (an admitted mission with populated scope and no guards reads as adoption under one gloss and non-adoption under another); es#166's own finding concerns declaration fields going empty, and permissions/protected_state are NOT census-reported, so they cannot enter a census-computable numerator.

preconditions.statement: The predicate's inputs are disjoint from the envelope fields whose population is being estimated.

residual_mismatch: The model treats adoption as a single ratio; a richer per-field measure would need its own derivation.

result.statement: Any envelope-referencing predicate (option D) makes the adoption window vacuous by construction, independent of estate state.

steps: Option D defines membership using envelope fields (guard_mode non-null, or scope non-empty).
Under D, every member satisfies the adoption criterion by construction, so p == 1 identically.
An estimator whose value is fixed by its own selection rule carries no information about the quantity it names.
Therefore D cannot distinguish an estate where adoption improved from one where it did not.

residual_mismatch: Detectability assumes the gate owner reads the root column rather than the ratio alone.
A steward that renames a scratch root to look like a repo root defeats the signature; the model does not cover deliberate root-name mimicry.

result.statement: No fully non-gameable predicate exists among census-computable properties; the achievable property is detectable gaming, which only the root-path condition supplies.

steps: Every census-computable candidate input (receipt_count, checkpoint count, root path) is produced by steward action.
Therefore no candidate predicate is strictly non-gameable by the measured party.
Options are distinguished not by immunity but by whether gaming leaves a detectable signature.
Root path carries such a signature: es#173 records the scratch-workspace detachment as a named, already-observed evasion pattern, and the census reports the root of every mission it counts.
Receipt count and checkpoint count carry no comparable signature: suppressing an effect or padding revisions is indistinguishable from ordinary work in census output.

basis: D is refuted outright by d1 (selection on the dependent variable) and independently fails d3 on current evidence.
B and C satisfy computability but fail d2's detectability property: neither constrains root, so the already-observed scratch-workspace evasion is invisible to the measurement.

An admitted-root set is itself operator-authored, so it moves the judgement from 'what is a scratch root' to 'which roots count' -- a smaller and auditable judgement, made once and on the record, but not the elimination of judgement.

The numerator field set (scope_in, scope_out, guard_count) is a judgement about which fields count as envelope adoption, made once and recorded, exactly like the admitted-root set. It is bounded by what the census reports: permissions and protected_state are named in es#166's finding but are not census-computable, so this numerator understates adoption of the envelope as a whole and measures only the reported subset.

Cadence bounds resolution, and the record does not pretend otherwise: an adoption and a disappearance that both fall between two observations are indistinguishable from no adoption at all. That residue is reported as unresolved attrition rather than silently absorbed into the numerator or the denominator.
conditions: The admitted-root set is recorded BEFORE observation begins, and the window does not open until it is.
The numerator predicate (scope_in non-empty OR scope_out non-empty OR guard_count > 0) is the one recorded here, and is not renegotiated after observation begins.
The non-emptiness test in empirical_closure passes against that recorded set.
The gate owner reads the per-mission root column, not only the aggregate ratio.

The OPENING COHORT is recorded at window open (mission id, root, lifecycle state), so a mission that disappears during the interval is visible as attrition rather than silently leaving the denominator.
The prerequisite run and the closing run both report answers_are_partial == false, or the window does not open / does not close on that run.
The readout states the ACTUAL observed interval (open date to close date), never the nominal 60 days. The 60-day figure describes the interval planned on 2026-08-14, not the interval observed.

If opening slips, the gate owner records BEFORE opening whether the shortened interval still supports a judgement, and on what reasoning. Deciding that after seeing the ratio is choosing the standard to fit the result.

If the prerequisite has still not passed at 2026-10-13, the window does not open retroactively and does not silently extend: non-passage is itself reported to es#166 as the direction-1 finding (no substantive missions to measure), which is the same recovery the empty-predicate case already carries.

The OPENING COHORT record captures each member's DENOMINATOR AND NUMERATOR state (mission id, root, lifecycle state, scope_in/scope_out non-emptiness, guard_count), not identity alone -- otherwise a member that disappears takes its adoption state with it and the surviving-subset ratio silently replaces the cohort ratio.

The cohort is RE-OBSERVED on a cadence fixed and recorded before observation begins, and every observation is persisted (per member: lifecycle state, scope_in/scope_out non-emptiness, guard_count). Each cadence observation also DISCOVERS AND ADMITS newly qualifying missions -- a mission created during the interval, or one that gains its first chain-bound receipt, enters the cohort at the observation that first sees it qualify. Re-observing only the opening members would contradict the model (the cohort is every qualifying mission observed at ANY point in the interval) and bias the ratio toward the opening population, which is the same survivorship error as closing on survivors, taken at the other end.
recovery_moves: If the non-emptiness test fails, the correct move is not a looser predicate but a finding that the estate has no substantive missions to measure — which is itself the answer to es#166 direction 1 (manifest is a file-shaped-work instrument).
Record the root list observed at window open, so a root-name change during the window is visible at close.

If the CLOSING denominator is empty despite a non-empty opening cohort, that is attrition, not absence: report the opening cohort and its fate rather than a ratio over zero. An undefined p is not evidence of non-adoption, and reporting it as one would be the vacuous-green defect this record has already committed once.

If a census run bearing on the measurement is partial, resolve or admit the skipped stores before re-running. Do NOT compute a ratio over the readable subset: the skipped stores are exactly the ones whose state is unknown, so the resulting p would be selectively incomplete in an unmeasurable direction.

PARTIAL attrition is governed, not only total: a cohort member OBSERVED adopting at any recorded observation counts in the numerator at close even if it later disappears. 'Observed' means a persisted observation -- the opening record or a recorded interval re-observation -- never an inference, because a member that adopts after opening and then disappears is invisible to both the opening record and the closing census. A member that disappears with no observation of adoption is reported as UNRESOLVED ATTRITION and is not silently dropped: dropping it moves the ratio (2 members, 1 adopted, the adopter vanishes: 1/2 becomes 0/1) in a direction nobody chose.

Whenever any cohort member has disappeared, the readout reports BOTH the full-cohort ratio and the survivor-only ratio, and states the gap. A missing member contributes its LATEST PERSISTED OBSERVATION to the full-cohort ratio, never its opening snapshot: a member that adopted after opening and then vanished is in the numerator by the partial-attrition rule, and computing the same ratio from opening state would exclude it -- one observation history yielding two numerators depending on which rule the reader followed. Reporting one number where two are defensible hides exactly the attrition this cohort record exists to expose.
